dedupe_keys.name: nenia germany wide industrial waste heat register and heat demand atlas

description: The NENIA project builds the first Germany-wide waste heat register of industrial sites, recording energy inputs and the theoretically usable quantities of waste heat by temperature, humidity, pollutant load and temporal availability, together with a heat demand atlas, so that waste heat can be matched to heating networks. Site data are processed, checked for plausibility and enriched with other sources such as the European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register. It is produced by the Institute for Energy and Environmental Research Heidelberg, GEF Ingenieur AG and Geomer GmbH, and described on energieforschung.de, the information site of the German federal energy research programme. Coverage is all of Germany. The partners developed a licence and usage agreement, and third parties can license the heat demand atlas from Geomer for any area of Germany, so access is paid and on request. Caveats: the page read is a project summary without data documentation, and waste heat quantities are theoretical potentials. For simulation it supports source-sink analyses of waste heat and heat demand at municipal or regional level, energy master planning and studies of district heating networks that rely on industrial heat. It is related to the BfEE Germany waste heat platform record in this catalogue, the federal reporting platform for waste heat.
